Stateful Economics: Effort Tuning vs. Model Switching
Path A · Keep Model & Tune Reasoning Effort (~90% turns in beta)
• Preserves warm input-token cache, avoids prefix rebuilds, keeps tool style
• Watch-out: higher effort can still be non-monotonic in cost and accuracy
Path B · Model Switch or Provider Failover (Cache Penalty)
• Intentional switch: triggered by repeat errors or failing tests after edits
• Hidden hazard: allow_fallbacks: true host failover also drops local cache
Disclosed Metrics vs. Snapshot Evidence Gaps (2026-11-06)
Verified Primary Scope · Routing Step & Beta Aggregates
• Routing p90: 1.96s -> 0.65s (routing step only, NOT 3x E2E speedup)
• Beta vs. old router: 4x fewer invalid tool calls, 0.5x cut-offs (no CI)
Heatmap Missing in Freeze · 5-Benchmark Claim Needs Audit
• Text claims Auto Code matches Claude Opus 5.5 at 74% lower cost/task
• HTML alt: Deep SWE, SWE-Atlas QA, Terminal Bench 4.0, τ³-bench, MMMU Pro
• Only official.png preserved; cell scores, N & Opus effort tier unverified

Methodological Check: Failure Prediction (arXiv:2611.08285)
• Shi & Assuncao (3,492 SWE-bench runs): pooled AUROC hides issue difficulty
• 522-issue pilot: post-hoc oracle (+10 pp) vs. half-split switch (+0.09 pp, CI~0)
• Same-model run variance = 42% (do not equate oracle pick with online gain)
